_comment: LONGER BUDGET (2000 steps, was 600): 1 stage x 4 blocks x 4 loops: ONE gate over a 4-block stack.
Both arms of this pair get 2000 steps, so the comparison stays paired.
WHY. At 600 steps the 2-gate arm was at in-distribution byte 0.603 against
the 1-gate arm's 0.854 -- it had not finished FITTING, let alone
transferring. Held-out 0.467 vs 0.748 therefore cannot be read as a
gate-structure effect yet, because underfitting masquerades as exactly
that. This repo has already retracted one conclusion built on an
undertrained pass (a 300-step fixed-batch run read as 'memorization onset
lies below 16 instances').
If the gap survives at 2000 steps it is the gate structure. If it closes,
the 600-step number was underfitting and was never a gate result.
Everything else is identical to the 600-step pair: d_model 96,
ffn_hidden 256, four distinct blocks, 16 block applications per token,
492,481 vs 492,578 parameters (the 97 being one extra gate head),
auto_batch FALSE, batch_size 6.
Rung: same-rule (subst-fst-fixed, k_set [0], k0_rate 1.0).
Run:
cargo run --example scaling_sweep -- \
research/experiments/stack-bps04x04.json depth gpu 4 \
